docs.title: ShareModule
docs.text: ShareModule is a wrapper around JAX/Equinox models that enables parameter sharing and provides utilities for model inspection and manipulation.

docs.title: Building Models
docs.text:
Use build_model() to turn your Equinox model into a spectracles model (a ShareModule). It accepts either a model instance, or the model class followed by its constructor arguments; the two are equivalent:

import spectracles as sp

model = sp.build_model(MyModel(shared_component=inner, ...))
model = sp.build_model(MyModel, shared_component=inner, ...)  # the same

build_model is also where sharing is detected: a component or parameter used in several places becomes one shared component or parameter. Don't construct a ShareModule directly.

docs.title: Parameter Paths
docs.text:
# Get all unique parameter paths (excludes shared duplicates and Known)
paths = model.get_parameter_paths()

# Include shared parameters
paths = model.get_parameter_paths(show_shared=True)

# Include Known parameters
paths = model.get_parameter_paths(show_knowns=True)

docs.title: Parameter Summary
docs.text:
# Print a rich table of all parameters
model.get_parameter_summary()

Shows path, shape, bounds, free/fixed status, and sharing info for each parameter.

docs.title: Sharing Summary
docs.text:
# Component-level: which modules are the same object
model.get_sharing_summary(level="component")
# Returns: {'line_1.v': ['line_2.v']}

# Parameter-level: which parameter values are shared
model.get_sharing_summary(level="parameter")
# Returns: {'line_1.v.coefficients': ['line_2.v.coefficients']}

docs.title: Model Tree
docs.text:
# Print the model structure
model.print_model_tree()

# Include sharing relationships
model.print_model_tree(show_sharing=True)

docs.title: Model Graph
docs.text:
# Plot the model as a directed graph
model.plot_model_graph()

# Component-level view (shared modules point to same node)
model.plot_model_graph(sharing_level="component")

# Parameter-level view (shows all paths)
model.plot_model_graph(sharing_level="parameter")

docs.title: Setting Values
docs.text:
# Set a single parameter
model = model.set("line_1.A.coefficients", new_value)

# Set multiple parameters
model = model.set(["path.to.param1", "path.to.param2"], [value1, value2])

docs.title: Fixing/Freeing Parameters
docs.text:
# Fix parameters (won't be optimized)
model = model.set_fixed_status(["path.to.param"], [True])

# Free parameters
model = model.set_fixed_status(["path.to.param"], [False])

# Fix all parameters
model = model.fix_all()

# Free all parameters
model = model.free_all()

docs.title: Evaluating Parts of a Model
docs.text:
Calling the whole model always works, with or without sharing:

prediction = model(data)

Calling a part of it needs care when that part contains sharing. A shared parameter is stored once, at its parent location; its other locations hold a Shared reference to it. That is what makes it one parameter: it is updated in one place (by set, an optimiser or the latent space) and every location sees the same value. But a submodule that holds such a reference can't be called on its own, because the reference is not a value:

model = build_model(TwoLines, line_1=Line(v=shared_gp), line_2=Line(v=shared_gp))
model.line_1(data)  # fine: line_1 holds the shared GP itself
model.line_2(data)  # RuntimeError: line_2 holds a reference to line_1.v

for_evaluation() returns a copy with every reference replaced by its value, so any part can be called or inspected:

evaluable = model.for_evaluation()
flux_2 = evaluable.line_2(data)
velocity = evaluable.line_2.v(grid)

The copy no longer tracks sharing, so use it for evaluation only (predictions, plots, checks), not for optimisation or to build a LatentSpace. Keep working with the original model for those. (get_locked_model() is the old name of for_evaluation() and is deprecated.)

docs.text:
from spectracles.priors import Laplace, LogNormal

model = model.with_priors(
    {
        "**.kernel.length_scale": LogNormal(0.5, 0.2),
        "offset.spaxel_values": Laplace(0.02),
        "line.σ_lsf.spaxel_values": "fixed",
    }
)
model.get_priors()  # {path: prior} for every parameter that has one

See Priors and inference for the full workflow.

# Check sharing structure is valid
info = model.validate_sharing()

Return a new model with parameters updated to be fixed or not based on provided paths and list of bools. Can only be used to update fixed statuses of Parameters or ConstrainedParameters. The model must not be locked.

docs.title: with_priors(spec)
docs.text:
Return a new model with priors set (or parameters fixed) by path or glob.

Patterns use the same glob syntax as build_schedule ('*' matches one path component, '**' any number). Values are a spectracles.priors.Prior or the string "fixed". Patterns are matched against all non-Known parameter paths, including shared ones: a shared parameter is one parameter, so a pattern on any of its paths sets that one parameter.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default spec dict[str, Any]

Mapping from path pattern to a Prior or "fixed".

required

Returns:

Type Description Self

A new ShareModule; the original is unchanged. Parameter values and

Self

free/fixed status are kept (except where "fixed" is given).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If a pattern matches nothing, if two patterns ask for different things on the same parameter, or if a prior is given for a ConstrainedParameter.

TypeError

If a value is neither a Prior nor "fixed".

Examples:

>>> model = model.with_priors({
...     "**.kernel.length_scale": LogNormal(0.3, 0.15),
...     "flux_cal.tile_values": Normal(0.0, 0.01),
...     "line.σ_lsf.spaxel_values": "fixed",
... })

Validate the sharing structure of the model.

Checks that: 1. All Shared objects reference valid parent parameters 2. Parent parameters exist and have the expected shape 3. No orphaned Shared objects exist 4. All locations of a shared parameter have the same fixed status and prior

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default raise_on_error bool

If True (default), raises ValueError on validation failure. If False, returns validation results without raising.

True

Returns:

dict[str, Any]

docs.title: copy()
docs.text: Create a proper copy of the ShareModule with correct sharing structure preserved and duplicated array data. It's like deepcopy but preserves the sharing structure.

docs.title: for_evaluation()
docs.text:
A copy of the model for evaluating any part of it.

In a model with sharing, each shared value is stored once, at its parent location; its other locations hold Shared references to it. That is what keeps a shared parameter one parameter, but it means a submodule containing such a reference can't be called on its own. In the copy returned here every reference is replaced by its value, so any submodule can be called, e.g. model.for_evaluation().line_2.v(data).

The copy no longer tracks sharing, so it is for evaluation only: it can't be optimised or used to build a LatentSpace. The model itself is unchanged; calling it (model(data)) never needs this.

docs.title: Fitting a GP field with VI, NUTS and MAP
docs.text:
A complete example of the priors and inference workflow, end to end:

  1. Simulate data from a known log-normal field.
  2. Fit it with MGVI (NIFTy.re).
  3. Fit the same posterior with NUTS (BlackJAX) and MAP (optax).
  4. Compare the field from the three.

It runs on a laptop CPU in about a minute. The figures on this page are produced by this code (docs/examples/make_figures.py regenerates them).

docs.title: The model and simulated data
docs.text:
A field f(x, y) is a Matérn-3/2 Gaussian process, observed at 500 random points as d = exp(f) + noise. It is a stand-in for a line-flux map.

import equinox as eqx
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
from jax import random

from spectracles import FourierGP, Matern32, Parameter, SpatialDataGeneric, build_model
from spectracles.inference import GaussianLikelihood, LatentSpace, Posterior
from spectracles.priors import LogNormal

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)


class LogGP(eqx.Module):
    gp: FourierGP

    def __call__(self, data):
        return self.gp(data)


kernel = Matern32(
    length_scale=Parameter(prior=LogNormal(0.6, 0.2)),
    variance=Parameter(prior=LogNormal(1.0, 0.5)),
)
model = build_model(LogGP, FourierGP(kernel, n_modes=(15, 15)))
latent = LatentSpace(model)

N = 500
k_xy, k_truth, k_noise = random.split(random.PRNGKey(0), 3)
xy = random.uniform(k_xy, (2, N), minval=-jnp.pi, maxval=jnp.pi)
points = SpatialDataGeneric(x=xy[0], y=xy[1], idx=jnp.arange(N))


def forward(m):
    return jnp.exp(m(points))


# The truth is a draw from the prior, hyperparameters included
truth = latent.sample_prior_latent(k_truth)
noise = 0.05
data = forward(latent.to_model(truth)) + noise * random.normal(k_noise, (N,))

posterior = Posterior(latent, forward, GaussianLikelihood(data, jnp.full(N, noise**-2)))

docs.title: MGVI
docs.text:
import nifty.re as jft

from spectracles.nifty import to_nifty

lh = to_nifty(posterior)
n_iterations = 15  # fast in tests: 3
k_init, k_vi = random.split(random.PRNGKey(1))
samples, _ = jft.optimize_kl(
    lh,
    jft.Vector(lh.init(k_init)),
    key=k_vi,
    n_total_iterations=n_iterations,
    n_samples=4,
    sample_mode="linear_resample",  # "nonlinear_resample" for geoVI
    kl_kwargs={"minimize_kwargs": {"maxiter": 20}},
)
posterior.summary(samples, true_latents=truth)  # with the truth, since we simulated the data

To see the field, evaluate each sample on a grid:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

n = 100
g = jnp.linspace(-jnp.pi, jnp.pi, n, endpoint=False)
gx, gy = jnp.meshgrid(g, g, indexing="ij")
grid = SpatialDataGeneric(x=gx, y=gy, idx=jnp.arange(n * n))

f_true = latent.to_model(truth)(grid).reshape(n, n)
f_mgvi = posterior.draws(samples, to="model")(grid).values.reshape(-1, n, n)  # per sample

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 3.4), layout="constrained")
lim = float(jnp.abs(f_true).max())
panels = [
    (f_true, "truth", {"cmap": "RdBu_r", "vmin": -lim, "vmax": lim}),
    (f_mgvi.mean(0), "MGVI mean", {"cmap": "RdBu_r", "vmin": -lim, "vmax": lim}),
    (f_mgvi.std(0), "MGVI std", {"cmap": "viridis"}),
]
for ax, (img, title, kw) in zip(axes, panels):
    im = ax.imshow(np.asarray(img).T, origin="lower", extent=(-np.pi, np.pi, -np.pi, np.pi), **kw)
    ax.plot(xy[0], xy[1], "k.", ms=1, alpha=0.3)
    ax.set_title(title)
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.85)
fig.savefig("inference_fit.png", dpi=100)
plt.close(fig)

docs.title: NUTS on the same posterior
docs.text:
BlackJAX samples posterior.log_density directly, in the same latent coordinates. Starting from the MGVI mean saves warm-up time. This is a short run, to show the mechanics. Real NUTS runs on GP models need long chains and convergence checks (see How it works).

import blackjax

n_steps = 200  # fast in tests: 20
k_warm, k_draw = random.split(random.PRNGKey(2))
warmup = blackjax.window_adaptation(blackjax.nuts, posterior.log_density)
(state, params), _ = warmup.run(k_warm, samples.pos.tree, num_steps=n_steps)
nuts_step = jax.jit(blackjax.nuts(posterior.log_density, **params).step)


def one_step(state, key):
    state, _ = nuts_step(key, state)
    return state, state.position


_, nuts_samples = jax.lax.scan(one_step, state, random.split(k_draw, n_steps))

docs.title: MAP with optax
docs.text:
import optax

optimiser = optax.adam(0.05)
ξ_map = latent.zeros()
opt_state = optimiser.init(ξ_map)


@jax.jit
def step(ξ, opt_state):
    grad = jax.grad(lambda x: -posterior.log_density(x))(ξ)
    updates, opt_state = optimiser.update(grad, opt_state)
    return optax.apply_updates(ξ, updates), opt_state


n_map_steps = 500  # fast in tests: 20
for _ in range(n_map_steps):
    ξ_map, opt_state = step(ξ_map, opt_state)
map_model = latent.to_model(ξ_map)

docs.title: Comparing the field
docs.text:
All three results are latents of one posterior, so the same latent turns each into a model. Here is the field at the data points:

f_nuts = posterior.draws(nuts_samples, to="model")(points).mean()
f_mgvi_pts = posterior.draws(samples, to="model")(points).mean()
f_true_pts = latent.to_model(truth)(points)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.5, 4), layout="constrained")
ax.plot(f_true_pts, f_mgvi_pts, ".", ms=3, label="MGVI mean")
ax.plot(f_true_pts, f_nuts, ".", ms=3, label="NUTS mean")
ax.plot(f_true_pts, map_model(points), ".", ms=3, label="MAP")
lims = [float(f_true_pts.min()), float(f_true_pts.max())]
ax.plot(lims, lims, "k-", lw=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel("true f at the data points")
ax.set_ylabel("estimate")
ax.legend(fontsize=8)
fig.savefig("inference_compare.png", dpi=100)
plt.close(fig)

The three methods recover the field consistently. Comparing uncertainties and GP hyperparameters between methods needs much longer runs than this example; see How it works.

docs.title: Schedule Builder Examples
docs.text: Practical examples of using the schedule builder API.

docs.title: Basic: Single Parameter
docs.text:
Optimize a simple model with one parameter:

import spectracles as sp
import jax.numpy as jnp

# Build model
model = sp.build_model(MyModel, value=1.0)


# Loss function
def loss_fn(model, x, y):
    return jnp.mean((model(x) - y) ** 2)


# Single phase, single parameter
schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model,
    loss_fn,
    phases=[(100, 0.1)],
    params={
        "param": sp.free_in(0),
    },
)

schedule.run_all(x=x_data, y=y_data)
final_model = schedule.model_history[-1]

docs.title: Staged Optimization
docs.text:
Common pattern: warm up some parameters first, then refine others.

schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model,
    loss_fn,
    phases=[
        (200, 0.1),  # Phase 0: High LR warm-up
        (100, 0.01),  # Phase 1: Lower LR refinement
        (50, 0.001),  # Phase 2: Fine-tuning
    ],
    params={
        # Coefficients: optimize throughout
        "*.coefficients": sp.free_in(0, 1, 2),
        # Kernel parameters: freeze during warm-up
        "*.kernel.lengthscale": sp.free_after(1),
        "*.kernel.variance": sp.free_after(1),
        # Noise: only fine-tune at the end
        "noise": sp.free_in(2),
    },
)

docs.title: Reinitializing Parameters
docs.text:
Sometimes you want to reset a parameter partway through:

import jax.random as jr

schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model,
    loss_fn,
    phases=[
        (100, 0.1),  # Phase 0
        (100, 0.1),  # Phase 1: restart amplitude
        (50, 0.01),  # Phase 2
    ],
    params={
        "gp.coefficients": sp.free_in(0, 1, 2),
        # Reset amplitude to random values at phase 1
        "line.amplitude": sp.free_in(0, 1, 2) | sp.init_normal(1, mean=0.0, std=0.5),
        # Set width to specific value at phase 1
        "line.width": sp.free_after(1) | sp.init_value(1, 1.0),
    },
    key=jr.key(42),  # Required for init_normal
)

docs.title: Wildcard Patterns
docs.text:
Match multiple parameters with glob patterns:

schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model,
    loss_fn,
    phases=[(100, 0.1), (50, 0.01)],
    params={
        # All coefficients in any submodule
        "*.coefficients": sp.free_in(0, 1),
        # All kernel parameters (lengthscale, variance, etc.)
        "*.kernel.*": sp.free_after(1),
        # Any parameter named 'noise' at any depth
        "**.noise": sp.free_in(1),
    },
)

docs.title: Pattern Reference
docs.text: Pattern Matches "param" Exact match "gp.kernel.lengthscale" Exact nested path "*.param" inner1.param, inner2.param "gp.*" gp.coefficients, gp.kernel, etc. "gp.*.lengthscale" gp.kernel.lengthscale, gp.spatial.lengthscale "**.lengthscale" Any lengthscale at any depth

docs.title: Using Different Optimizers
docs.text:
Override the default optimizer per-phase:

import optax

schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model,
    loss_fn,
    phases=[
        (100, 0.1),  # Uses default (adam)
        (50, 0.01, optax.sgd(0.01)),  # Explicit SGD
        (50, 0.001, optax.adamw(0.001)),  # AdamW with weight decay
    ],
    params={
        "*.coefficients": sp.free_in(0, 1, 2),
    },
    default_optimizer="adam",  # Default for phases without explicit optimizer
)

docs.title: Managed Schedule (Interactive)
docs.text:
Use ManagedOptimiserSchedule for more control:

schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model,
    loss_fn,
    phases=[
        (100, 0.1),
        (50, 0.01),
        (50, 0.001),
    ],
    params={
        "*.coefficients": sp.free_in(0, 1, 2),
        "*.kernel.*": sp.free_after(1),
    },
    managed=True,  # Returns ManagedOptimiserSchedule
)

# Run phases one at a time
schedule.run_next_phase(x=x_data, y=y_data)
print(f"Phase 0 done, loss: {schedule.loss_history[-1]:.4f}")

# Check status
print(schedule.get_phase_status())

# Skip a phase if needed
schedule.skip_phase(1)

# Run remaining
schedule.run_all(x=x_data, y=y_data)

# Reset and try again with different data
schedule.reset()
schedule.run_all(x=new_x, y=new_y)

docs.title: Shared Parameters
docs.text:
When parameters are shared, only specify the parent path:

# If model has sharing: line_2.amplitude -> line_1.amplitude
# Only specify the parent path

schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model,
    loss_fn,
    phases=[(100, 0.1)],
    params={
        "line_1.amplitude": sp.free_in(0),  # Parent path
        # "line_2.amplitude": ...           # Don't specify - it's shared!
    },
)

# Check available paths if unsure:
print(model.get_parameter_paths(show_shared=False))  # Parent paths only
print(model.get_parameter_paths(show_shared=True))  # All paths

docs.title: Full Example: Spectral Line Fitting
docs.text:
import spectracles as sp
import jax.numpy as jnp
import jax.random as jr

# Build a spectral-spatial model
model = sp.build_model(
    MySpectralModel,
    n_spatial=64,
    n_spectral=100,
)


def loss_fn(model, data):
    pred = model(data)
    return jnp.mean((pred - data.flux) ** 2)


# Three-phase optimization strategy
schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model,
    loss_fn,
    phases=[
        (500, 0.05),  # Phase 0: Establish spatial structure
        (200, 0.01),  # Phase 1: Refine line parameters
        (100, 0.001),  # Phase 2: Polish everything
    ],
    params={
        # Spatial coefficients: always free
        "spatial.*.coefficients": sp.free_in(0, 1, 2),
        # GP kernel: freeze initially, then optimize
        "spatial.*.kernel.*": sp.free_after(1),
        # Line amplitudes: reinitialize at phase 1
        "lines.*.amplitude": sp.free_in(0, 1, 2) | sp.init_normal(1, std=0.1),
        # Line positions: fix until final polish
        "lines.*.center": sp.free_in(2),
        # Line widths: optimize from phase 1
        "lines.*.width": sp.free_after(1) | sp.init_value(1, 1.0),
        # Continuum: always free
        "continuum.*": sp.free_in(0, 1, 2),
    },
    key=jr.key(0),
)

# Run optimization
schedule.run_all(data=my_data)

# Get result
final_model = schedule.model_history[-1]
